title: Redwood POC weekly sync - benchmark review vs baseline provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark numbers vs baseline provider, discuss tuning options (batching, KV cache, quantization), and align next steps for a production pilot. Redwood shows lower p95 latency and higher throughput on our test workload; customer asks for end-to-end tests with simulated traffic and security docs.
topics: Next steps: load tests, security doc share, pricing
action_items: Alex Chen: Share detailed benchmark spreadsheet and raw logs by 2026-05-14
Priya Patel: Run 50k-step simulated load test and share results by 2026-05-19
Tom Rivera: Provide production traffic sample and target SLOs by 2026-05-15
next_steps: Redwood to send full benchmark CSV and test harness link
Customer to approve load test run in their staging VPC
Schedule 1-hour results review the week of 2026-05-19
Redwood to share SOC2 and network diagram
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-12
Time: 10:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Mills (Redwood Support), Tom Rivera (Nimbus CTO), Sara Li (ML Eng), David Kim (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick numbers review, questions on noise, ask for end-to-end run, agree next steps.

[00:00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we will run about 30 minutes of benchmarks and then Q A, keep questions in chat, priya will run through the slides and numbers.
[00:00:23] Priya Patel: Cool, hi. so quick re-cap of test setup — model is redwood-13b-quant-v2 (approx), sequence length 512, batch sizes varied 1-16, request pattern simulates our snippet generation workload, tokenization as your prod sample. baseline provider run was done using customer-provided harness last week.
[00:00:48] Tom Rivera: quick clarification, baseline was Bedrock run on g5i equivalent right? that's what sara ran.
[00:00:56] Sara Li: yeah we ran Bedrock with their managed endpoint using the default concurrency we had, i added a note in the sheet.
[00:01:15] Priya Patel: ok great, top-level numbers p50,p95 and throughput first. Redwood hosted config (our test) p50 = 38 ms per token (actually per request median 120ms), p95 = 210 ms, throughput 220 rps at 95% CPU of the node pool for the pattern. Baseline p95 was about 410 ms and throughput around 150 rps. those are median of three runs.
[00:01:50] David Kim: those are pretty material numbers. can you remind us what exact batching policy you used for that 220 rps number?
[00:02:02] Priya Patel: sure — continuous batching enabled, max batch 16, latency target 200ms, and we used prefix caching for repeated calls to the same prompt families, kv cache warm-up enabled for the run. small note: cache hit rate was 62% for this workload, so effective perf looks better.
[00:02:30] Tom Rivera: the cache part i want to be careful about — our prod has lot of ad-hoc prompts so cache hit may be lower. how sensitive is throughput if cache hit drops to 20%?
[00:02:45] Priya Patel: good question — in an offline sensitivity run we saw throughput drop from 220 rps to ~170 rps when cache hit goes to 20%, and p95 increases to ~320ms. i'll attach that sheet.
[00:03:05] Alex Chen: also worth calling out quantization profile — the 13b was int8-ish, that helped reduce memory and get better kernel throughput versus baseline, which we think ran fp16 by default.
[00:03:20] Sara Li: can you remind me, is your runtime doing KV cache across requests for multi-turn? we have some long conversations and that matters.
[00:03:30] Priya Patel: yes we maintain KV cache per session and we stream back tokens, the run used per-connection KV, so multi-turn was represented. if you have long histories the effective latency per request is lower because cached prefix is not re-computed.
[00:03:50] [00:04:05] Jordan Mills: quick aside — we had a small transcription glitch in the logs where model name was munged, ignore that.
[00:04:15] Tom Rivera: about dedicated vs hosted — these numbers are for hosted right? what's the delta if we go dedicated (reserved pool) with larger instance types?
[00:04:30] Priya Patel: dedicated gives two improvements: more predictable tail latency because of isolation and you can tune kernel selection and quantization more aggressively. in an internal dedicated run on a 8xA100 equivalent we saw p95 drop to ~160ms and throughput to 320 rps for the same workload. that's a best-case number with higher memory and fewer noisy neighbors.
[00:05:00] David Kim: network e2e matters — baseline had higher e2e because they were in a different region and more hops. did you normalize for region?
[00:05:10] Priya Patel: we ran both in us-west-2 and used the same egress path when possible. there may still be infra differences but we used curl-based pings and removed fixed network overhead from the per-request numbers. raw logs will show the offsets.
[00:05:35] Alex Chen: quick callout on cost — rough unit cost per 1k tokens was about 0.09 on our test config vs baseline ~0.13 after accounting for caching and batching. we'll include price sensitivity sheet.
[00:05:50] Sara Li: great. any gotchas on regulatory/security? we need SAML/SSO and audit logs — you have SOC2 right?
[00:06:06] Alex Chen: yes SOC2 Type II, plus SAML SSO and audit trails. we'll share our security pack and network diagram after this meeting.
[00:06:20] Tom Rivera: can you run an end-to-end run from our staging VPC? we want to see with our ingress rules and longer tails.
[00:06:30] Priya Patel: absolutely, we'll need a short window and a service account from you. propose next thursday 2026-05-20 for a 2-hour run.
[00:06:45] Tom Rivera: sounds good. we'll provision a test service account and send keys.
[00:07:00] [00:07:15] Priya Patel: a couple of more detail points — we saw some variance at high concurrency due to tokenization cost on very long prompts, if you can trim pre-prompt length or move to pre-encoded prefixes it helps.
[00:07:35] Sara Li: noted. also curious about model fallbacks — earlier you mentioned automatic fallback to smaller variants, is that per-route?
[00:07:45] Alex Chen: yes, our routing policy can default to a lower-cost compatible model under heavy load; you can configure per-route and SLOs for automatic fallback.
[00:07:58] David Kim: in the rough numbers you presented, what's the perf of the fallback model?
[00:08:05] Priya Patel: fallback 7b quantized had p95 ~95ms and throughput ~480 rps in the same cluster, but obviously quality will vary so we recommend evaluation prompts to validate.
[00:08:30] Tom Rivera: ok let's talk noise and variance — were these single zone runs? and how many warm-up iterations did you do?
[00:08:40] Priya Patel: single AZ, 3 warm-up runs of 500 requests each, measurement run was three 10-minute sustained windows per config. we logged individual request timestamps.
[00:08:58] Sara Li: excellent — can you share the raw request logs? we want to run our own analyzers.
[00:09:05] Alex Chen: yes raw logs will be in the sheet link, we can provide S3 access or CSV.
[00:09:15] [00:09:30] Priya Patel: quick mention, quantization may change exact tokens in edge cases; we did an eval on 2000 prompts and quality delta was <1.2% on Rouge/Exact-match approximations for your use-case.
[00:09:50] Tom Rivera: that is acceptable ballpark. any risks if we move to on-prem/private later?
[00:09:58] Priya Patel: Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem stacks, there will be some ops time to tune kernels and batchers but performance is similar once tuned; we can scope that as a later phase.
[00:10:15] David Kim: another security question — does caching persist to disk or only in-memory? we need to avoid persisted sensitive prefixes.
[00:10:25] Jordan Mills: caching is in-memory only by default, and you can disable prefix caching per-route for sensitive workloads. we'll add that to the security note.
[00:10:40] Priya Patel: ok moving on, open questions from your side?
[00:10:50] Sara Li: just one — in the sensitivity sweeps did you test with lower batch max (like 4)? curious how p95 behaves at small batch.
[00:11:00] Priya Patel: yes at max batch 4, p95 rose to ~270ms and throughput dropped to ~180 rps for same load, which suggests moderate batching is optimal for your pattern.
[00:11:20] Tom Rivera: timeline — if we approve the end-to-end run next week, how long until you can give us a full pilot SLA and contract?
[00:11:30] Alex Chen: assuming results align to the runs, we can draft a pilot agreement and reserved capacity terms in 2 weeks, so target 2026-05-26 for a first draft.
[00:11:45] Tom Rivera: good. i also want to make sure we get an apples-to-apples baseline — looks like your baseline was Bedrock default, can we re-run baseline with identical batching and caching disabled to ensure parity?
[00:11:58] Priya Patel: yes we can coordinate that, but note some providers don't expose the same kernel-level tunables; we'll try to match higher-level knobs: batch size, concurrency, sequence length.
[00:12:15] [00:12:30] Jordan Mills: small note on logs — there is an identifier mismatch in one run where the session IDs were hashed differently; ignore run #2 in the attached CSV, run #1 and #3 are clean.
[00:12:45] Sara Li: thanks.
[00:12:50] Tom Rivera: any other blockers from your side?
[00:12:55] Priya Patel: just permissions for the staging run and a small headcount from your infra team for troubleshooting in the window.
[00:13:10] Tom Rivera: i'll allocate david and one of infra for that window.
[00:13:20] Alex Chen: perfect. final quick recap of agreed next steps: we'll send benchmark CSV, run a sensitivity sweep with cache hit 20% scenario and share, coordinate staging VPC run on 2026-05-20, and provide security docs.
[00:13:40] Sara Li: sounds good.
[00:13:45] Tom Rivera: thanks everyone, appreciate the data; looking forward to the staging run.
[00:13:55] Alex Chen: thanks, we'll follow up in email with the attachments.
[00:14:05] Meeting end notes: call ran 45m, lots of alignment and clear owner list for next steps.

(Transcription notes: occasional mis-heard product names and timestamps; speaker labels approximate.)
